full_judgment:
Mohammad Ullah, J: On an application under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondents show cause as to why the initiative taken by the respondents to transfer the ownership of the private car of the petitioner, bearing No. "Dhaka Metro-Gha:15-5914" (said car) ignoring her objection should not be declared to be without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and as to why the respondents should not be directed to stop harassing the petitioner asking to appear repeatedly at the office of the respondent No.2 on the pretext of resolving the disputes of ownership of the said car and/or why such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper shall not be passed. 

 2. The facts relevant for the disposal of the Rule as made out in the writ petition, in short, are that the petitioner by her hard earned money purchased a private car bearing Chassis No. RU1-1012694, Engine No. L15B-3512710. Pearl Colour and got her name registered on 4-5-2017 bearing registration No. "Dhaka Metro Gha:15-5914" (hereinafter referred to as the disputed car). Due to the frequent misbehaviour of her husband at one stage she was compelled to leave the husband's residence keeping her private car, and the documents of the car therein. Without obtaining any permission her husband on 22-2-2018 deposited the requisite money to the bank for transferring the ownership of the car in his name. Having heard such an initiative, the petitioner on 27-2-2018 applied to respondent No. 2 requesting him not to transfer the ownership of the car to her husband's name (Annexure-B). Respondent No. 2 by a letter dated 30-7-2018 asked the petitioner to appear personally at his office on 27-8-2018 to give statements about the dispute of the ownership of the car and accordingly, she appeared therein and explained the total situation and requested respondent No. 2 not to transfer the ownership of the car (Annexure-C). In this connection, the petitioner also made a CD Entry to the police station. Again on 7-1-2019 the respondent No. 2 asked the petitioner to appear in person at his office within 7(seven) days, to explain the ownership of the car and informed that if she fails to appear and explain her position that deemed to be she has had no objection in changing the ownership of the car. She on 10-1-2019 again appeared at the office of respondent No. 2 and put her specimen signature. Thereafter the petitioner on 14-1-2019 sent an application to respondent No. 2 informing that all the documents of the car remained with her husband's house and she did not put her signature on the purported document of changing the ownership of the car and requested not to transfer the ownership of the car (Annexure-E). Again on 29-1-2019, respondent No. 2 issued a letter asking the petitioner to appear at his office within 7(seven) days with a money receipt, import document and other relevant papers in connection with the car. In such facts and circumstances, the petitioner on 9-2-2019 served a legal notice upon the respondents stating the facts that she having repeatedly appeared in the office of the respondent BRTA requesting them not to transfer the ownership of the car. Despite such facts again on 15-7-2019, respondent No. 2 issued another notice asking the petitioner to appear personally at his office on the pretext of resolving the dispute about the transfer of the ownership of the car which manifests the bad intention of the respondents to transfer the ownership of the car to her husband's name and harassment of the petitioner (Annexure-H). 

 4. Respondent No.3, husband of the petitioner contested the Rule by filing an affidavit-in-opposition and supplementary affidavit-in-opposition contending, inter alia, that he purchased the car from his fund. But the petitioner managed the registration of the car to her name through the backdoor as a result she is trying to avoid the BRTA authority. The BRTA being a statutory authority has lawful responsibility to resolve the dispute in respect of the ownership of the car. The dispute about the registration of the car does not fall within the purview of the fundamental rights guaranteed under Articles 27, 31 and 42 of the Constitution and, as such, the writ petition is not maintainable. Who paid the purchased money of the car is a highly disputed question of fact that cannot be resolved under the summary jurisdiction of this Court. Under section 107 of the Road Transport Act, 2018 there is a provision for review against any order of BRTA and since the petitioner without availing the alternative remedy filed the instant writ petition, the Rule should be discharged. 

 5. Respondent No. 2, BRTA entered appearance through Mr Muhammad Rafiul Islam, a learned Advocate of this Court who filed an affidavit-in-opposition stating, inter alia, that the BRTA has the authority to transfer the ownership of the car in question and to do its statutory obligation, BRTA asked the petitioner to appear in person and there is no intention on the part of the office of the BRTA to harass or humiliate the petitioner in any way. The BRTA issued a circular under Memo No. 35.03.0000.31.041.2015-1367 dated 26-4-2016 stating the fact that for transfer of ownership of a car legally, the owner of the car should come to the office of BRTA personally and disclose his or her identity and make a signature on the transfer document. Accordingly, the petitioner was asked to appear at the office of the BRTA. Under section 24 of the Road Transport Act, 2018, the BRTA has the authority to cancel the registration of any vehicle and, as such, notices, as issued upon the petitioner to resolve the dispute, was legally served and hence the Rule should be discharged. 

 6. On the written request of respondent No. 3 the BRTA took initiative to transfer the ownership of the car that deposited the requisite transfer fees to the concerned bank on 22-2-2018. Based on the application filed by the petitioner. BRTA suspended data front the IS system of BRTA temporarily. Following the application dated 27-8-2018 filed by respondent No. 3, respondent No. 2 by a letter dated 7-1-2019 asked the petitioner appear in person at his office to give her statement about transferring the ownership of the car. On the said request made by respondent No. 2, the petitioner on 27-2-2018 and 10-1-2019 personally appeared before respondent No. 2 and put her specimen signature to show that the purported affidavit for transferring the ownership of the car as filed by respondent No. 3 is forged one. On 28-1-2019 the respondent No. 2 asked the petitioner to appear before his office in person to show the import documents but the petitioner neither appears in person nor submitted any document of the car. Respondent No. 2 only took initiative to resolve the dispute of ownership of the car and, as such, he did not harass the petitioner in any way. 

 7. Mr Khan Ziaur Rahman, learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that the car in question purchased by the petitioner from her fund and registration thereof made in her name rightly by the office of the BRTA, and the petitioner being the sole owner of the car without her written consent BRTA cannot take any initiative to transfer the ownership of the car and, as such, the initiative of the respondents taken beyond the provisions of law and Rules ignoring the objection of the petitioner and hence such initiative is liable be declared have been taken without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

 8. The learned Advocate submits further that on two occasions on the request of BRTA, the petitioner personally appeared and made her statements of ally, as well as, in writing and therein requested respondent No. 2 not to transfer the car to her husband's name but the respondent No. 2 did not pay any heed to such request of the petitioner rather repeatedly upon issuing notices tried to harass and disturb the petitioner in the name of resolving the dispute of the ownership of the car and, as such, the subsequent attempt of the respondent No. 2 should be declared to have been done without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

 9. The learned Advocate next submits that respondent No. 3 without obtaining any written affidavit or document for transfer of the ownership of the car as required by law deposited the transfer fee on 22-2-2018 to the concerned bank for transferring the car to his name and hence the respondent No. 2, BRTA cannot proceed further for transferring the ownership of the car ignoring the objection of the petitioner and, as such, the subsequent initiative as taken by the respondent No. 2, BRTA should be declared to have been made without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

 12. Mr NM Ahsanul Haque, learned Advocate for respondent No. 3 submits that respondent No. 3 paid the purchase money of the car from his fund, however, due to the restriction to get registration in joint name the car was registered in the name of the petitioner and, as such, the BRTA rightly took initiative to transfer the ownership of the car. 

 17. It appears from the facts that due to frequent inflexible and maladaptive patterns of behaviour, the petitioner was compelled to leave her husband's house on 5-2-2018. Maladjustment affects their couple relationship and family life and now they are living at a separate match. It appears from Annexure-A that the disputed car is registered in the name of the petitioner. The husband of the petitioner on 22-2-2018 deposited the requisite money for transfer the ownership of the car without any document from the petitioner. On the written notices, the petitioner appeared before respondent No 2 twice and explained the conduct of her husband and requested not to transfer the ownership of the car and she disclosed the facts that she did not put any signature in any document for transfer of the ownership of the car even though the responder` No. 2 repeatedly asked the petitioner to appear in person. In such facts and circumstances, when the BRTA ignoring the objection of the petitioner took further initiative without any no objection of the petitioner for transfer of the ownership of the car she moved this Court and obtained the Rule. At the time of issuance of the Rule, on 23-7-2019 the respondents were restrained by an order of injunction from transferring the ownership of the car. For transfer of the ownership of a car, BRTA is to confidently sanguine that the initiative to transfer has been taken properly and lawfully. If necessary BRTA can hear the owner of the car and proposed buyer in person. In the instant case, the petitioner on two occasions on the written requests of respondent No. 2 went to his office and made a written objection for not to transfer the ownership of the car. The petitioner expressed that she did not sign in any ownership transfer document. The affidavit for the transfer of the car dated 20-11-2018 is a forged one. Respondent No. 3 deposited the requisite transfer fees to the concerned bank on 22-2-2018 without oral or written consent for transferring the ownership of the car of the petitioner. Therefore, without no objection or written approach of the owner of the car, the BRTA cannot take further initiative to transfer the vehicle in favour of respondent No. 3. The learned Advocate for respondent No. 3 rightly submits that who paid the money is a disputed question of fact and sitting under writ jurisdiction this Court cannot determine such dispute. Accordingly, we need not consider it prudent to find out who paid the money to purchase the car in question. But there is no doubt the car was registered in the name of the petitioner and she is the sole owner of the car until or unless the ownership is transfer lawfully. Had respondent No. 3, the husband paid the purchased money of the car in favour of the petitioner even then the respondent No. 3 cannot claim the ownership of the car as there is no provision for Benami transaction. To the query made by this Court, the learned Advocate for respondent No. 3 submits that his client did not obtain any affidavit or transfer of ownership document from the petitioner. About Annexure-11 an affidavit for transfer of the ownership of the car as filed by BRTA, respondent No. 3 did not know anything. So it is manifestly clear that the petitioner did not file any affidavit for transfer of her car in favour of respondent No. 3. In such facts and circumstances, the petitioner filed a GD Entry No.358 dated 6-2-2019 to the Officer-in-Charge, Ramna Model Police Station, DMP, Dhaka.
